title: Salary Calculator Aus: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay (38-Hour Week)
description: Use our salary calculator aus to convert hourly pay to annual salary. See tax, super, and fortnightly pay for a 38-hour week. Free tool for Australian workers.
salarySummary: For a full‑time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is the hourly rate multiplied by 38 then by 52.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply that by 52. For a standard full‑time role, we assume 38 hours per week. So annual gross ≈ hourly × 38 × 52. Your fortnightly pay is roughly weekly pay × 2.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading rate?
faqs.a: The casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour; with casual loading it becomes $33.05 per hour. Our salary calculator aus has a checkbox to add this loading automatically.

faqs.q: Does superannuation count as part of my salary?
faqs.a: No. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. It is not included in your take‑home pay or in the annual gross figure shown by the calculator.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

Welcome to the **salary calculator aus** – your straightforward tool for turning an hourly rate into an annual figure. Whether you’re comparing a job offer, checking your current pay, or planning your budget, understanding how hourly pay translates to yearly earnings is essential. This article explains the simple maths behind the conversion, covers the key Australian benchmarks like the National Minimum Wage and award rates, and walks you through tax, superannuation, and the differences you might see across states.

## How the Hourly to Annual Conversion Works

The core formula is: **annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For a full‑time employee, we assume a standard 38‑hour week as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. If you work part‑time or have a different roster, simply substitute your usual weekly hours.

For example, an hourly rate of $30.00 gives:
- Weekly pay: $30.00 × 38 = $1,140.00
- Fortnightly pay: $1,140.00 × 2 = $2,280.00
- Annual gross: $1,140.00 × 52 = $59,280.00

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It’s a clean starting point for your own estimates.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission is **$26.44 per hour**, which equates to **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual minimum rate **$33.05 per hour**.

Many workers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets a higher minimum rate. Award rates vary by industry and classification. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) provide detailed rates for your specific job. If you’re not covered by an award, the National Minimum Wage applies.

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you type your base hourly rate and optionally add the 25% casual loading with a checkbox. **Never type a rate that already includes casual loading** – the calculator adds it for you.

## Tax and Superannuation

### Income Tax (2026–27 Resident Rates)

The Australian Taxation Office applies a progressive tax scale for residents:
- Nil tax on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies to your taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted in this estimate.

### Superannuation Guarantee

Employers must pay superannuation of **12% of your ordinary time earnings** on top of your gross pay. This amount is not deducted from your salary; it’s an additional contribution. The super guarantee is capped at the maximum contribution base of **$270,830 per year**. For earnings above that, no further super is required.

For a full‑time worker on $30.00 per hour (annual gross $59,280), the employer would contribute an extra $7,113.60 per year in super. This is shown separately in our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) reference.

## State Differences in Ordinary‑Time Earnings

While the National Minimum Wage is uniform across Australia, average earnings differ noticeably between states and territories. The Australian Bureau of Statistics’ *Average Weekly Earnings* survey for May 2026 reports:
- **Full‑time adult ordinary time earnings**: $2,083.70 per week nationally
- **All employees total earnings** (including part‑time): $1,579.20 per week

These are **averages**, not medians for any specific job. For example, full‑time workers in mining or professional services tend to earn above the national average, while those in retail or hospitality often earn below. State‑by‑state breakdowns show that New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory typically have higher average weekly earnings than Tasmania or South Australia.

If you are researching a particular occupation, the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides industry and state averages from the ABS. Remember that an average is not the same as a job median – your actual rate depends on your award, experience, and employer.

## Using the Salary Calculator Aus

Our [the timesheet](/) is the home page of the salary calculator aus. You simply enter your base hourly rate (the rate before any casual loading). If you are a casual employee, tick the checkbox to add 25% casual loading. The calculator then shows:
- Your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay
- An estimate of tax and Medicare based on the 2026–27 resident rates
- The superannuation contribution paid on top (12% of ordinary earnings, capped)
- An approximate take‑home figure (after tax and Medicare, before any other deductions)

For a more detailed breakdown including HELP repayments or salary packaging, see the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

## Important Notes and Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For official rates, always check the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page and the ATO’s tax tables. Use the salary calculator aus as a starting point, then consult your employer or a qualified professional for your exact situation.
